why: Three of the six API tests returned non-verdicts. On inspection each was a fault in the test instrument, not an unanswerable question. No threshold, criterion or fixture was changed, and no result was re-read after seeing an outcome: only the measuring apparatus was repaired, then every test was re-run once.

changes.fault: signal.interests.entities was set to candidates[0], which is the target itself. Qloo omits the signal entity from its own results, so the target went missing from a response and the test returned UNKNOWN without answering its question.
changes.fix: The signal is now a fixed entity outside the target and both candidate sets, so the only thing varying between the two calls is the candidate set, which is what the test is about.

changes.fault: The positive control was filter.popularity.min, which never moved the results. That control is circular: the finding under test is that this API swallows parameters it does not support, so a control that may itself be swallowed cannot show that the harness would notice a working parameter.
changes.fix: The control is now signal.location.query, which test F0 independently measured reordering an open query.

changes.fault: The test searched for the substring 'explain' in the first 4000 characters of each result. A film entity carries enough metadata to push query.explainability past that cut, so the test reported ABSENT while the product was reading the field successfully from the same response shape.
changes.fix: It now reads item['query']['explainability'] directly, the same field hero_build.py reads, and asks on both the open and the pinned query shape rather than only the open one.
